prompt:
Over the domain of all user accounts, A(u) means "u is an admin" and T(u) means "u has two-factor auth enabled". Which formula says **every admin has two-factor auth**?

*Symbols: ∧ means AND; → means "implies" (if ... then); ∀ means "for all"; ∃ means "there exists at least one".*

options.explanation: This says every account is an admin *and* has 2FA. Using ∧ with ∀ makes the claim about the whole domain, not just admins.
Correct. ∀ pairs with →: for each account, if it is an admin then it has 2FA. Non-admins satisfy the implication vacuously.
This requires at least one 2FA-enabled admin. The universal rule requires every admin to be 2FA-enabled and is vacuously true if no admins exist; the two statements differ.
This is the converse: every account with 2FA is an admin. It says nothing about admins without 2FA.

workedExample: Test the rule on a regular account without 2FA. A rule about admins must allow that account. An implication does, because its admin premise is false. Conjunction would wrongly require that account to be an admin as well.

prompt:
A compliance check is specified as there exists u (Admin(u) implies Verified(u)). It passes on a database with 1,000 **unverified** admins and one regular user. Why?

*Symbols: → means "implies" (if ... then); ∀ means "for all"; ∃ means "there exists at least one".*

options.text: The check is correct; at least one admin must be verified
options.explanation: No admin is verified here, so if it meant that, it should fail. The formula does not say what was intended.

options.text: Existential claims are always true over non-empty domains
options.explanation: there exists x P(x) is false whenever no element satisfies P. The issue is specifically the → inside ∃.

options.text: The regular user makes Admin(u) implies Verified(u) vacuously true, which is all ∃ needs
options.explanation: Correct. For the regular user, Admin(u) is false, so the implication is true and serves as a witness. ∃ should pair with ∧.

options.text: The database has more than one user, so ∃ becomes ∀
options.explanation: Quantifiers don't change with domain size. The check passed because of the shape of the formula, not the number of users.

workedExample: An existential check needs one witness. The regular user's admin predicate is false, so its implication is true regardless of verification. To require a verified admin, the witness must satisfy both properties together.
